DIRECTION CONCEPT SEED (key: oracle-key-2; mode: operate; source: local; catalog: phoenix-2026-01; approved pool: d79644e7d5df; 24/24 catalog-curated; rerun with --scope direction --mode operate --from oracle-key-2 --candidate-count 5 to reproduce this roll against this catalog revision)
ASSIGNED INDEX: 4
  After ordering the grounded directions by resonance, build candidate
  4 of your own grounded list; the assignment never points at a
  challenger. The assignment is the roll, not a suggestion: your top-ranked
  direction is what every run would ship, so the script decides which grounded
  direction gets built. Each direction joins a durable visual system to a
  concrete expression for the requested first surface, decided as one. It must
  survive the current task plus navigation, quiet and dense content,
  interaction and state, and a substantially different future surface. In an
  attended run, present the assigned direction fully committed and offer
  re-roll. You may add ONE card for your top-ranked grounded candidate when
  it is not the assigned direction, kicker PHOENIX UI PICK, with an honest risk line
  naming its familiarity; one pick card, never a ranked lineup, and the pick
  never takes the lead position. When the assignment IS your top candidate,
  there is no pick card. Re-roll yourself only
  on named factual grounds, when the assignment cannot carry the product's
  truth or task; taste is never grounds.
  The assignment exists to refuse the model's ranking rut, never to outrank
  the user or the brief. Never expose assignment metadata in user-facing labels.
CHALLENGERS:
  1. A located operations table, stable record labels and workspace context make dense rows navigable without losing the current task.
     SOURCE ID: phoenix-operate-density-location
     CREATIVE SPARK: A busy table stays calm when location is dependable: operators know which workspace and record they are changing after filtering, opening detail, or returning from an action.
     SYSTEM GRAMMAR:
       - Palette/material: Use a light neutral table field and dark text; reserve labeled status colors for operational meaning.
       - Type/composition: Align identifiers and quantities consistently; prioritize row labels over decorative summary metrics.
       - Topology/navigation: Keep workspace scope above the table and record identity beside detail; preserve the return location.
       - Controls/state: Expose sort, filter, selection, and loading states separately; keep row actions individually named.
       - Responsive/motion: Prioritize essential mobile columns; allow labeled overflow and retain location without animated shifts.
     WEB LEVERAGE: Use semantic table headers, labeled sort controls, tabular numerals, and a stable focus target after closing detail.
     MEDIA: text-only candidate; no local image supplied
  2. A traceable task state board, record identifiers, owners, deadlines, and transition history explain what each operational state means.
     SOURCE ID: phoenix-operate-traceable-state
     CREATIVE SPARK: Make state trustworthy through its visible path: operators can see who owns the work, what happened most recently, and which next transition is actually available.
     SYSTEM GRAMMAR:
       - Palette/material: Use a neutral board and thin dividers; use labeled state markers rather than many saturated card colors.
       - Type/composition: Prioritize record ID and task name; keep owner, due date, and last change in a predictable text rhythm.
       - Topology/navigation: Connect queue summary, task detail, and chronological history; distinguish current state from prior states.
       - Controls/state: Name permitted transitions and consequences; explain unavailable actions and avoid implicit state changes.
       - Responsive/motion: Convert lanes to labeled mobile lists; retain state grouping and provide still feedback after transitions.
     WEB LEVERAGE: Use semantic lists and time elements, accessible state labels, and explicit transition controls with immediate result confirmation.
     MEDIA: text-only candidate; no local image supplied
  3. A difference-centered approval view, current and proposed values align beside their scope, impact, and explicit approval decision.
     SOURCE ID: phoenix-operate-change-difference
     CREATIVE SPARK: Treat a proposal as a precise difference: reviewers can identify what changes, who or what is affected, and whether the preview remains current before reaching approval.
     SYSTEM GRAMMAR:
       - Palette/material: Use neutral comparison surfaces; additions and removals have text signs and accessible colors of equal visibility.
       - Type/composition: Align field names and old/new values; separate impact summary from approval action in the type hierarchy.
       - Topology/navigation: Place changed fields first, then dependencies and unchanged context; keep affected scope visible throughout.
       - Controls/state: Distinguish pending, approved, rejected, and outdated proposals; refresh the preview after source changes.
       - Responsive/motion: Stack labeled old and new values on mobile; avoid animated diffs that interfere with review or copying.
     WEB LEVERAGE: Use labeled comparison regions and accessible change summaries; do not rely on red and green alone to indicate changes.
     MEDIA: text-only candidate; no local image supplied
  4. An in-place reconciliation sheet, source values, proposed matches, and correction reasons remain adjacent during review.
     SOURCE ID: phoenix-operate-reconcile-place
     CREATIVE SPARK: Make a reconciliation decision explainable by keeping its evidence beside it: inspect a source, amend a suggested match, and record a concrete reason without changing screens.
     SYSTEM GRAMMAR:
       - Palette/material: Use white data surfaces and restrained blue selection; label amber mismatches with readable contrast.
       - Type/composition: Align source and target values by field; give conflicting values equal readable weight before any recommendation.
       - Topology/navigation: Connect unmatched records, proposed matches, and evidence; retain the active row when editing.
       - Controls/state: Separate unmatched, suggested, confirmed, and failed states; do not silently replace original source data.
       - Responsive/motion: Stack matched pairs by field on mobile; provide immediate edit feedback without unexpectedly moving corrected rows.
     WEB LEVERAGE: Use labeled field pairs, accessible edit forms, preserved row focus, and an explicit validation summary for failed corrections.
     MEDIA: text-only candidate; no local image supplied
  5. An exception-first monitoring summary, actionable abnormal states dominate while normal counts provide stable operational context.
     SOURCE ID: phoenix-operate-exception-summary
     CREATIVE SPARK: A monitoring overview answers where attention is needed now: quiet normal totals provide scale while each exception identifies an affected object, data freshness, and a useful next action.
     SYSTEM GRAMMAR:
       - Palette/material: Use a quiet neutral field; apply restrained severity colors only with readable labels and symbols.
       - Type/composition: Place actionable exceptions above compact normal totals; use tabular values without oversize decoration.
       - Topology/navigation: Order exceptions by declared severity and time; connect each to scope, evidence, and a useful next action.
       - Controls/state: Distinguish acknowledged, resolved, stale, and unknown data; show refresh time and preserve manual investigation.
       - Responsive/motion: Prioritize exception detail on mobile; update counts without flashing, surprise resorting, or ornamental motion.
     WEB LEVERAGE: Use accessible status summaries, visible timestamps, polite update announcements, and links to concrete investigation records.
     MEDIA: text-only candidate; no local image supplied
  6. A scoped batch action preview, affected records and consequences are inspected before one explicit commit with recoverable failure detail.
     SOURCE ID: phoenix-operate-batch-preview
     CREATIVE SPARK: A bulk action earns confidence through a specific preview: operators know which records will change, can cancel before commitment, and can recover from partial failure without guessing.
     SYSTEM GRAMMAR:
       - Palette/material: Use neutral work surfaces and one strong action accent; destructive actions carry text and restrained warning color.
       - Type/composition: Give selected count, scope, and consequence summary distinct headings; keep individual failures readable.
       - Topology/navigation: Separate selection, preview, commitment, and result; return to the same records after cancellation or failure.
       - Controls/state: State whether hidden records are selected; retry failed items and promise undo only when actually supported.
       - Responsive/motion: Keep commit and summary connected on mobile; report progress without blocking access to result detail.
     WEB LEVERAGE: Use grouped selection controls, a labeled confirmation region, accessible progress, and per-record retry actions in the result list.
     MEDIA: text-only candidate; no local image supplied
Fuse each challenger before judging it: the challenger supplies the form
  and its system grammar, the product supplies every fact, and clarity wins
  conflicts. Weigh the fused result against the assigned direction on exactly
  two axes, audience identification and product clarity. Losing to strong
  grounded material is a valid outcome; beating a thin or tool-monoculture
  list is the point. A fused challenger that wins both axes becomes the build.
  Close the weighing with a verdict per challenger, decided before any
  borrowing is considered: wins (beats the assigned direction on both axes),
  competitive (holds one axis), or declined (loses both). A declined
  challenger is not spent: name the one discipline of its system the assigned
  direction lacks, and raise the assigned direction to match before
  presenting it. A donation transfers ambition and system discipline, never
  the challenger's clothes; one world owns the page. Write each raise as its
  own named line on the presented direction, and carry every verdict, kept
  line, and raise into the decision page payload.
Compare supplied local images only when they exist. A text-only candidate has no visual reference; do not invent a board or contact a remote image service.
PRODUCT.md and explicit incumbent brand commitments constrain every direction.
The seed never chooses exact colors, fonts, tokens, or a user preference, and
it never permits the world and first surface to be selected independently.
The CREATIVE SPARK is a complete visual system, not a theme or decorative
reference. Translate every supplied system rule into the product: palette and
material, type and composition, topology, controls and states, and adaptation.
Keep the source's visible character, scale, rhythm, and interaction instead of
reducing vivid grammar to generic nouns. Keep a literal carrier only when it
becomes functional.
Ambitious motion, spatial media, or interaction is welcome when it strengthens
the product without weakening semantics, performance, or fallback behavior.
MODE RULES (operate, from <REPO>/tests/fixtures/mode-rules-skill/reference/mode-operate.md). They govern this surface's directions and every comp you write or judge for it, the decision comps included; where shared guidance conflicts, these win.
